newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil JV funding meeting set for August 6.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil JV funding meeting set for August 6.

text.p: A meeting between Nigeria's joint venture oil production partners and senior government officials to discuss a funding crisis will be held on August 6, the petroleum ministry said on Wednesday.
"The chief executives of the oil companies will attend, and so will officials from here and from other ministries," a spokesman for the petroleum ministry said in the capital Abuja.
The meeting was originally scheduled to take place last week, but government sources said officials from the finance ministry did not turn up. They did not give a reason.

Oil industry officials say Nigeria's current production, of more than two million barrels per day, could be cut by as much as five percent in 1997 if an increase to their funding is not approved. They say long term effects would be even more serious.

The joint venture partners complain they have been forced to cut back new projects, maintenance and exploration after an across the board cut to $2.05 billion from a proposed $3.32 billion budget for 1997.
